text:
Predicates:
City(x) ::: x is a city.
InState(x, y) ::: x is in state y.
State(y) ::: y is a state.
InU.S(x) ::: x is in the U.S.
SameState(x, y) ::: x and y are in the same state.
DifferentState(x, y) ::: x and y are in different states.
DistinctCities(x, y) ::: x and y are distinct cities.
InCity(x, y) ::: x is in city y.
Premises:
City(butte) ∧ InState(butte, montana) ∧ State(montana) ∧ InU.S(butte) ::: Butte is a city in Montana, U.S.
City(helena) ∧ InState(helena, montana) ::: Helena is a city in Montana.
City(missoula) ∧ InState(missoula, montana) ::: Missoula is a city in Montana.
City(whiteSulphurSprings) ∧ InState(whiteSulphurSprings, montana) ::: White Sulphur Springs is a city in Montana.
City(stPierre) ∧ ¬InState(stPierre, montana) ::: St Pierre is not in Montana.
∀x (InCity(x, butte) → InState(x, montana)) ::: Any city in Butte is in Montana.
∀x (InCity(x, stPierre) → ¬InState(x, montana)) ::: Any city in St Pierre is not in Montana.
∀x, y (InCity(x, y) ∧ InCity(z, y) ∧ x ≠ z → x ≠ z) ::: A city can only be in one state.
∀x, y, z (InCity(x, y) ∧ InCity(x, z) → y = z) ::: A city is in only one state.
Question:
Butte and stPierre are in the same state?
